A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenTSLM. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, memory-scaling simulations, generated model examples, and a cardiologist evaluation of ECG rationales.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of Chronos-2 encoder variants and a fine-tuned image baseline.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an alternative feature-extraction and training path using a frozen pretrained time-series foundation model with a trainable projection, demonstrated with Chronos-2 in OpenTSLM-Flamingo. V1 used encoders trained from scratch. The original fusion architectures and language-modeling objective remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use TSQA, M4-Captions, HAR-CoT, Sleep-CoT, ECG-QA-CoT, and the same synthetic memory-scaling scenarios. The added configurations reuse existing benchmarks without expanding task or population coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds Gemma3-4B FT, fine-tuned on plot inputs, across all four benchmarks. Existing comparators remain. Newly discussed methods such as ChatTS and ITFormer are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce frozen pretrained-encoder configurations and a fine-tuned plot-input condition. Existing dataset splits, metrics, training limits, and the 84-example cardiologist-review protocol remain unchanged; Appendix A.1 states that Chronos-2 variants retain the scratch models' learning rates.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Table 3 add a systematic encoder-component comparison between scratch encoders and Chronos-2 across four LLM backbones and four benchmarks. V1 lacked this analysis. Existing memory-scaling analyses, failure examples, and clinician assessments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 42 for GPT-4o rationale generation and report the same reviewer-disagreement analysis. V2 adds no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedure for model performance.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for four Chronos-2 configurations and the fine-tuned image baseline, whose TSQA/HAR/Sleep/ECG F1 scores are 94.94/44.01/18.56/26.17. Original Table 2 scores and appendix memory and reviewer results remain unchanged. The encoder comparisons include regressions: Gemma3-1B-pt Flamingo achieves HAR F1 62.72 with Chronos-2 versus 65.44 with its scratch encoder.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same patch encoding, projection, fusion, and autoregressive-loss formulations. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the pretrained-encoder extension introduces no new formal derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the contribution to integration with pretrained time-series foundation models. The abstract also changes the fine-tuned HAR baseline from 52.2% to 60.44%, matching the existing Table 2. The central two-architecture, three-dataset, and memory-scaling claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the encoder results as supporting reuse of pretrained foundation models. Its limitations remove the explicit caveats about absent ablations and untested unseen-data generalization, replacing them with the limitation that only Chronos-2 was evaluated. No unseen-data generalization experiment is added.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the Chronos-2 checkpoint source and documents frozen encoder parameters and retained learning rates. Conversely, it replaces the repository link with a double-blind-review placeholder and removes the detailed reproducibility statement covering weights and clinician-annotated notebooks. General release claims remain; actual resource availability cannot be inferred from these edits.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to cover ChatTS, ITFormer, InstructTime, and MedTsLLM, including new Table 1 entries. New Section 2.4 positions OpenTSLM relative to Chronos-2, TimesFM, and Moirai2, distinguishing forecasting foundation models from language-generating reasoning systems.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and encoder explanation, condenses the main memory discussion, adds two subsections, and removes the reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Authorship and affiliation text also change. The overall section sequence and most existing prose and appendix content remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references adopt a two-column layout, Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 4 is rearranged into a 2-by-2 grid. Tables are resized and expanded, a new results table appears, and v1 Figure 5 moves to appendix Figure 18. The main sleep example panel is removed, but the same example remains in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The fine-tuned plot baseline provides a more informative comparison, while Table 3 tests an important encoder choice absent from v1. Expanded related work also strengthens positioning. These gains are partly offset by removal of the unseen-data generalization caveat and reduced resource-access disclosure; details and uncertainty reporting for the new experiments remain limited.
